title: The Deadline of the Free Port
premise: Dominic Crane, a financial-crimes investigator who launders her own past behind a polished lie, discovers her secret safe house listed for sale online — complete with photos of its interior, including documents she never photographed. The listing is a message: someone inside her agency sold her out, and the buyer is a laundering network planning to destroy a free-port summit with a staged industrial accident. Forced to work with the one colleague who suspects her double life, Dominic must trace the money to the bomb while deciding whether loyalty to the institution that betrayed her matters more than the truth. In the end she stops the attack, exposes her handler as the leak, and walks away from the agency with her go-bag finally unpacked — choosing truth over the survival she'd been rehearsing for years.
about_author: Rosalind Ishikawa spent a decade auditing shipping manifests in port cities before turning to fiction, a career that left her fluent in the grammar of offshore money. She writes from a coastal apartment she refuses to photograph.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Scrolling real-estate listings at 2 a.m., she finds her own safe house for sale — interior photos showing her forged passports on the kitchen table. She burns the go-bag's contents, then realizes the photos include a document only her handler ever saw. Emotional beat: the sick vertigo of a polished lie cracking open.

chapters.title: Clean Money, Dirty Hands
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. At the financial-crimes unit, she quietly pulls the listing's brokerage records while presenting a routine case. The shell company behind the sale routes through the free-port zone hosting next month's trade summit. Her colleague Ada Okonkwo catches the query and says nothing. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Handler
chapters.summary: Dominic confronts her handler, Marcus Vey, who denies leaking the photos but warns her off the summit file with unusual urgency. She notices his cufflinks — a gift matching the brokerage's parent firm. POV shifts briefly to Ada, who files a quiet flag on Dominic's records search. Emotional beat: the loneliness of not knowing who to fear.

chapters.title: The Buyer's Agent
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. She poses as a buyer to meet the listing agent in the free port, and finds the 'agent' is a logistics coordinator for a maritime services firm with no sales history. She photographs his ledger; he photographs her back. Emotional beat: hunter and hunted realizing they're the same thing.

chapters.title: What Ada Knows
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada has traced Dominic's off-book queries and confronts her in a parking garage, offering a deal: full honesty for her silence. Dominic gives half the truth — the safe house, not the passports. Together they map the network's money into the summit's security contractor. Emotional beat: wary alliance, the first warmth in the book.

chapters.title: Accident, Scheduled
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The money trail reveals a 'maintenance contract' on the summit venue's fuel depot — insurance policies taken weeks ago against an 'accidental' explosion timed to kill the anti-corruption delegation. The network isn't attacking the summit; it's eliminating the people who could expose it. Emotional beat: cold dread becoming a countdown.

chapters.title: Vey's Ledger
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. She breaks into Vey's office and finds he's been paid to steer her investigation away from the depot — but the payments originate above him, from the agency's own oversight director. Vey catches her, and instead of arresting her, begs her to run. Emotional beat: betrayal compounded; the mentor unmasked as another hostage.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada discovers Dominic's forged identities and must choose: report her or cover for her. She covers, but demands they go to the summit's host-nation liaison together — meaning Dominic's lie dies in daylight. Meanwhile the depot contract moves up its schedule. Emotional beat: the price of loyalty paid in truth.

chapters.title: Detonation Window
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Summit eve. Dominic infiltrates the depot posing as the maintenance crew's auditor, finds the ignition rig disguised as a sensor array, and is trapped by the coordinator from chapter four. She stalls him with the one weapon she has — the ledger proving his own employers plan to erase him too. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into leverage.

chapters.title: The Free Port
chapters.summary: Dominic and Ada's alternating POV. The rig is disarmed minutes before the delegation arrives; the oversight director is arrested when Vey, choosing truth at last, hands over his ledger. Dominic testifies under her real name — the forged ones retired — and walks out of the agency with Ada, the go-bag empty on her shelf. Emotional beat: survival redefined as something you stop rehearsing and start living.
